title: Pauser can sandwich pause/unpause cycles to lock specific stakers into pauseWithdraw (forfeiting rewards) while others claim normally -- selective denial of yield
rootCause: The Pauser role (a mutable sibling, treated as trusted per profile §6) can pause and unpause at will, with no time-bounds, no quorum, no reason field. While paused: `stake`, `withdraw`, `claim` revert; `pauseWithdraw` works (and forfeits rewards per ECON-011 / CODE-009). The Pauser thus has unilateral economic power over WHEN stakers can claim, and consequently which stakers absorb the V1 asymptotic decay vs benefit from a freshly-funded collectReward injection. Coordinated pause/unpause cycles can selectively benefit pauser-aligned stakers and disadvantage others, without any on-chain 'fairness' check.
economicImpact: Strategic Pauser actions can: (a) freeze claims after a `collectReward` injection so the per-share value grows during pause, then unpause to allow pauser-aligned stakers to claim disproportionate amounts before others realize -- a pause-and-snipe; (b) pause during a user's planned exit window, forcing them to either wait indefinitely or take `pauseWithdraw` and forfeit rewards (per ECON-011, those rewards become orphaned). The Pauser effectively becomes a yield arbiter with no on-chain accountability.
affectedParties: All stakers (subject to Pauser discretion); the protocol's 'permissionless yield' narrative; trust in the Pauser sibling.
attackScenario: Pauser observes a `collectReward(large)` lands. `accStablePerShare` jumps. Aligned-staker has a big position; misaligned stakers also benefit.
Pauser calls pause(). All stakers are now frozen out of `claim()`.
Misaligned stakers face a choice: wait (with no SLA) or call pauseWithdraw and forfeit pending rewards.
Aligned-staker (assumed to be coordinated with Pauser) waits because they trust the unpause timing.
Pauser unpauses after a strategically-chosen interval. Aligned-staker claims, captures the post-collectReward value. Misaligned stakers who took pauseWithdraw lose proportionally.
Variant: if the pauser is the same entity as the stable-yield-accumulator funder, they can fund -> pause -> wait -> unpause and selectively pay only known-friendly addresses.
profitability: Bounded by the size of pending rewards at the moment of pause and the pause duration. Realistic upper bound: the value of `rewardBalance` distributed during the locked window, prorated by aligned-staker share.
preconditions: Pauser address is set to a non-zero address.
Pauser can act adversarially or in coordination with specific stakers.
The Pauser sibling's governance is weaker than this finding assumes (the profile §6 treats Pauser as trusted, but trusted-but-coercible is the threat model here).

intentMismatchEvidence.documentation: Profile §6: 'pauser - sibling Global Pauser (mutable dep). Out-of-scope implementation; treated as a trusted operator able to pause this contract at any time.' The trust label is profile-level, not a user-facing guarantee.
intentMismatchEvidence.implementation: No rate limit on pause/unpause, no min-duration, no max-duration, no per-staker fairness mechanism (e.g. allow `claim` during pause for users who entered before the pause).
intentMismatchEvidence.discrepancy: A 'pause' in DeFi is usually framed as a safety mechanism, not a selectivity mechanism. The protocol's framing implies pause is rare and protective; the implementation allows it to be frequent and selectively economic.

mitigations: Allow `claim()` to work during pause for users whose `stake` predates the pause (i.e. exempt pre-pause positions from `whenNotPaused` on claim).
Enforce a minimum unpause-cooldown so frequent pause cycles are limited.
Require multi-sig or timelock on the Pauser role at the sibling layer (out of scope for this contract but a documented dependency).
Emit per-pause/unpause events with reason codes so external monitoring catches anomalous cycles.
crossReferences: CODE-009 (pauseWithdraw forfeiture) - amplifier: the more often pauses happen, the more times users face the forfeit-or-wait choice.
ECON-011 (orphan reward redistribution) - amplifier: each pause-induced pauseWithdraw orphans more reward share.
